intentions.title: Render one PortableDoc block tree to two structurally different, byte-locked outputs — a semantic classed article DOM for the paper reader/editor and an inline-styled, table-based email skin for stylesheet-less mail clients — from a single compose/walk pass
intentions.evidence:
compose.ex: nearly every compose_block/2,3 clause has an :article branch (semantic

/

    ) and a default/email branch (inline PdBox/PdText scaffolds, e.g. list items become flex-row spans with literal '• '/'1. ' prefixes because 'Outlook strips
      padding'); walk.ex moduledoc states the DATA-vs-THEME contract explicitly: article emits bare elements styled by Stylesheet, email is frozen inline HTML 'byte-identical to the pre-palette walker'.

intentions.title: Keep every non-article render surface (email, bare export) working with zero shared stylesheet by threading a resolved palette/theme (colors, fonts, widths) through compose+walk instead of relying on CSS
intentions.evidence: palettes.ex: email_palette/1 and article_palette/1 build fully resolved literal color/font maps from TokensGen; article_palette wraps every value in var(--paper-*, <hex>) so it degrades to the same hex when rendered outside .bp-paper-surface (paper.html.heex, email backend); compose.ex @default_theme :evergreen note: 'the evergreen default makes compose_block(b, style, :evergreen) byte-identical to compose_block(b, style)'.

intentions.title: Never let a malformed, unknown, or type-mismatched block crash the render pipeline — degrade every leaf/table/heading field and every unrecognized block type to a visible fallback instead of a 500
intentions.evidence: compose.ex stringish/1 coerces non-binary author fields to '' rather than raising Protocol.UndefinedError; compose_block(%{'type' => type}, _style) and the final compose_block(_other, _style) catch-all both degrade to an escaped 'Unsupported block' / 'invalid block' div citing 'Papers are schemaless, so any raw API/SDK/CLI mutate can persist a block type this engine has no clause for'; image block with empty src composes to '' rather than a broken .

intentions.title: Keep the Elixir HTML renderer and the Go pdrender TUI renderer as parity twins driven by the same golden fixtures and the same manifest/token sources, so a paper looks/behaves consistently whether read in a browser or a terminal
intentions.evidence: compose.ex moduledoc: 'Its cross-runtime twin is the block-composition step of the Go internal/pdrender renderer (held in parity by the shared golden fixtures)'; util.ex safe_url doc names parity twins web/lib/safe-href.ts and internal/pdrender/inline.go; status_vocab.ex reads design/status-manifest.json at compile time so 'sibling surfaces...derive from the SAME file via scripts/status-manifest-check.sh'; layout engine comments describe the TUI COLLAPSING grid→stack since 'a terminal has no grid'.

intentions.title: Never let content author input (URLs, hex colors, HTML-significant characters, block field values) escape into unsafe HTML — sanitize every leaf through one owned escape/URL-allowlist path
intentions.evidence: util.ex escape_html/1 escapes & < > " ' in fixed order to avoid double-escaping; safe_url/1 allowlists http/https/mailto/tel + root-relative/in-document paths and rejects protocol-relative //host, defaulting unsafe hrefs to '#'; compose.ex routes every field-* value/label/type through escape_html/escape_attr/safe_hex/safe_url before it reaches HTML.

intentions.title: Keep task/status vocabulary (glyphs, spinner roles, labels) single-sourced from the repo-root design manifest so the paper renderer, CSS tone tokens, and eventually Go/web surfaces can never drift on what a task status looks like
intentions.evidence: status_vocab.ex reads design/status-manifest.json at compile time via @external_resource, precomputes glyph/spinner/label/meaning-by-role maps, and is tagged '@canonical capability:status-vocabulary' — moduledoc: 'there is no second copy to keep in sync.'

intentions.title: Support a growing library of rich, editable content widgets (tasks, task-detail, task-board, roadmap, cards, notes, pipeline, stages, terminals, columns, data-viz stat/heatmap/chart, sheets, forms, diagrams, asciicasts) each with matched article and email renderings, without breaking byte-identical output for existing papers
intentions.evidence: compose.ex has dedicated clauses and _email_html twins for every widget family (FleetEmail, CardsEmail, PanelsEmail, DataViz, Components), each annotated 'ADDITIVE: the legacy X clause above is UNTOUCHED' or 'byte-identical to before'; forms.ex renders questionnaire/grill blocks as render-only <fieldset> markup with no script/action wiring, deferred to 'a later phase'.
